lines.text: Paul resolves to go to Jerusalem through Macedonia and Achaia, then to see Rome, and sends Timothy and Erastus ahead.
Silversmith Demetrius tells the craftsmen that Paul has persuaded many people in Asia to turn away.
The enraged men shout, the crowd drags Gaius and Aristarchus into the theatre, and the disciples stop Paul from going.
The Jews push Alexander forward, but the crowd shouts "Great is Artemis" for about three hours.
The clerk calms the crowd, sends complaints to the synagogue, warns of a rioting charge, and dismisses the assembly.
